doc.title: Monthly Updates [June]
doc.html:
INFO These update threads only contain major updates. If you're interested in seeing all minor changes you can follow our Commits Page on GitHub or Updates Channel in Discord.

Wiki Updates

  • All guides written by Dan, like /coffee/ & /pool/, have been compiled in /danfmhy/.

  • You can now search FMHY using Brave Goggles.

  • Added Nintendo, Sony, and Resource sections to ROMs.

  • Added Rubik's Cube, Minesweeper, and Crossword sections to Puzzles.

  • Added a Game Learning section to Educational, with Rubik's Cube + Chess subsections.

  • Added a Firefox Tools section to Internet.

  • Added a Data Breach Monitoring section to Privacy.

  • Added a Task Automation section to System Tools.

  • Added a Unix-Like section to the bottom of Linux.

  • Added Size Limits + Sign-up Requirements to Remote Torrenting descriptions.

  • Re-organized Android Audio Players based on Poll Results. The four stars are now: Poweramp, Musicolet, VLC, and foobar2000.

  • Re-organized Android Keyboards based on Poll Results. FUTO managed to keep its top spot, and Heli was bumped up much higher.

  • Re-organized Live Sports, removed sites w/ broken or dupe players, and starred a few that seemed to stand out. Before vs. After.

  • Re-organized Radio Streaming + Internet Radio, added new stars and new labels, and moved both sections out of storage.

  • Re-organized RSS Readers, improved labels, and removed bad ones. Before vs. After.

  • Re-organized Text Adventures, added labels, and moved out of storage. Before vs. After.

  • Re-organized Dev Tool Sites, moved out of storage, and separated into Indexes + Online Toolkits. Before vs. After.

  • Updated grading criteria #4 and #5 to reward sites that have source auto-switch + episode auto-next working across all their servers. Also merged quality, subtitle, and media type criteria into #1 to simplify scoring, and started giving points for watch party support. This has reduced the total amount of stars and helped the best sites stand out more. Before vs. After.

Stars Added ⭐

  • Starred LMArena in Image Gen. Good models, unlimited, no sign-up required; clear cookies if you're getting errors.

  • Starred HuggingChat in Online Chatbots. Privacy-friendly, lots of models, sign-up required, but temp-mail works.

  • Starred Blip in File Transfer. Easily transfer large files over the internet or between your own devices. Well-liked by everyone in our Discord who has tried it.

  • Starred ImageToolbox in Android Image Editors. Open-source, feature-rich, and well-maintained.

  • Starred Parabolic in YouTube Downloaders. Open-source, multi-platform, and one of the easier-to-use yt-dlp frontends.

  • Starred Infinite Backlog in Game Tracking / Databases. Backloggd/Glitchwave competitor with a nice UI, achievement integration, and challenges.

  • Starred GameBanana in Game Mods. High-quality, well-organized, and the go-to for certain franchises like Sonic, Celeste, etc.

  • Starred TETR.IO in Multiplayer Browser Games. F2P multiplayer Tetris that's popular, feature-rich, and well-maintained by its devs.

  • Starred Mario Kart PC in Browser Games. SNES-style Mario Kart w/ Custom Maps & Multiplayer.

  • Starred RootlessJamesDSP in Android Audio Equalizers. Open-source, supports many apps, AutoEQ support; good Poweramp alt.

  • Starred Plonk It in GeoGuessr Games. Active community for learning GeoGuessr.

  • Starred Zed in Coding AIs. Collaborative coding AI getting positive attention from HackerNews + our members.

Things Removed

  • Unstarred OOMoye as their library seems a lot smaller now, and their search is still broken.
